params.body:
Phase 2 of `docs/design/sources-before-more-sources.md`, first platform.

## An actor chosen by running it

The old actor (`clockworks~tiktok-trends-scraper`) had returned nothing since
12 May while ending every run `SUCCEEDED`. The Apify store shows that same actor
at nearly 100% success: the store's rate is the vendor's status, which is exactly
the lie. So the candidates were trial-run on 20 September under a $0.25 ceiling
each, eight cents in all:

| actor | result |
|---|---|
| `data_xplorer~tiktok-trends` | 10 real hashtags for FR in 5s, $0.025 |
| `khadinakbar~tiktok-trending-hashtags-scraper` | the same top three for FR |
| `automation-lab~tiktok-trends-scraper` | German hashtags when asked for Belgium |

Two actors agreeing on `#valouzz`, `#pronote`, `#frenchcreators` is what makes
the first believable. The second is named in the adapter as the **reserve**.

## What the adapter now holds to

- **Belgium and the Netherlands are not asked for, and that is TikTok's doing.**
  Both working actors report Creative Center publishes no trends for BE or NL any
  more. The row in `sources` still names them; the adapter skips them and says so
  every round, so nobody has to rediscover it.
- **"Top Creators" is never read.** It carries nicknames, handles, follower
  counts and avatars of individuals, and this system holds trend-level data only.
  A test fails if any trace of a person reaches a signal.
- **The text is a contract.** `getRecentTrendTerms` finds TikTok's terms by
  "Hashtag Trending" and "#name" followed by a long dash, and Instagram and Reddit
  search seed from it. The test goes through the real reader, not a copy of its
  regex.
- **A dead upstream stops the loop.** On 19 September asking five more countries
  is what hid the real reason behind "cut off after 150s".

## A cadence

A seven-day list does not change by the hour; every round was 45 runs a day.
`meta.cadence = {everyHours: 20}` lets the collector rest an adapter after it
**did its work**, and try again next round when it did not. Resting is not a run
and writes no row in `adapter_runs`: eight invented "skipped" rows a day would
bury the one that matters. About $4.50 a month, what the dead actor already cost.

## Switched off, with reasons

- **Pinterest**: not rented, on purpose. The actor is unchanged since April and
  never delivered; two candidates need no rental and get a trial run first.
- **Snapchat**: the store offers profile and Spotlight scrapers, individual
  content, not trend-level data.

783 tests pass, 9 new. After merge: one `collect.mjs --only=tiktok` on the box to
see the first signals since 12 May, and Instagram and Reddit search following.
params.title: TikTok comes back, on an actor chosen by running it
